Run the taxonomic matching pipeline

dot-run_matching_pipeline.Rd

The batch-exact cascade followed by per-name fuzzy matching, with checkpointing so an interrupted run can resume. Pure computation: give it the same inputs and it returns the same results, in this process or any other.

Usage

.run_matching_pipeline(
  user_df,
  col_name,
  backbone,
  min_similarity,
  include_authors,
  input_hash,
  rm_mode = "fresh",
  checkpoint_file = NULL,
  cancel_file = NULL,
  progress = NULL
)

Arguments

user_df

data.frame. The user's table.

col_name

Character. Column of `user_df` holding the names to match.

backbone

data.frame. Shaped backbone, from `.shape_backbone()` or `load_backbone_cache()`.

min_similarity

Numeric in 0-1. Fuzzy matching threshold.

include_authors

Logical. Match on authorship as well as name.

input_hash

Character. Identifies the run, from `.compute_input_hash()`.

rm_mode

Character, "fresh" or "resume".

checkpoint_file

Character path for the checkpoint. Passed explicitly because a worker process has its own `tempdir()` and would otherwise write its checkpoint somewhere the parent can never find.

cancel_file

Character path polled for cancellation, or NULL.

progress

Function called as `progress(stage, i, n, name)`, or NULL.

Value

A list with `status`: * `"ok"` — plus `updated_data`, `best_matches` and `stats` * `"empty"` — the chosen column held no names * `"cancelled"` — `cancel_file` appeared mid-run; the checkpoint is current
